```{r}
library(ggplot2)
# gerando vários pontos com coordenadas (x,y) para plotar no gráfico da curva da Normal 
#coord_x <- runif(1e3, min = 0, max = X) #eixo X
#coord_y <- runif(1e3, min = 0, max = 1/sqrt(2*pi)) #eixo Y

#coords <- matrix(c(coord_x,coord_y),ncol=2,byrow=F)

fdp_norm <- function(x, media=0, sigma=1) (1/(sqrt(2*pi*(sigma^2))))*exp(-0.5*((x-media)/sigma)^2)

#is_in <- apply(coords, 1, function(x) x[2]<=fdp_norm(x[1]))

ggplot()+
  #geom_ribbon(aes(x=xs, ymin=ysmin, ymax=ysmax), data=data.frame(xs = seq(-5,X,0.01), ysmin=0, ysmax=sapply(seq(-5,X,0.01), FUN= dnorm)), fill="cyan", alpha=0.5)+
  #geom_rect(aes(xmin=0, xmax=X, ymin=0, ymax=1/sqrt(2*pi)), fill="black", color=NA, alpha=.15)+
  #geom_point(data=data.frame(coords), aes(x=X1,y=X2, color=is_in), size=0.6)+
  geom_function(fun = dnorm, args=list(mean=1.5,sd=1.6), lwd=1.5, color="red", alpha=1)+
  geom_function(fun = dnorm, args=list(mean=-1.5,sd=1.4), lwd=1.5, color="grey", alpha=1)+
  geom_function(fun = dnorm, args=list(mean=0,sd=1), lwd=2, color="gray7", alpha=1)+
  #geom_function(fun = dbeta, args=list(shape1=1,shape2=.3), lwd=1, color='red')+

  #geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype="dashed", color="grey60")+
  #geom_hline(yintercept = 1/sqrt(2*pi), linetype="dashed", color="grey60")+
  #scale_y_continuous(expand = c(0,0), limits=c(0,.45))+ 
  theme_void()+
  scale_x_continuous(limits=c(-5,5))
```

```{r}
# Define the range of x values
x <- seq(-4, 8, length.out = 200)

# Define the parameters for the first normal distribution
mean1 <- 1
sd1 <- 0.5

# Calculate the y values for the first normal distribution using dnorm
y1 <- dnorm(x, mean = mean1, sd = sd1)

# Define the parameters for the second normal distribution
mean2 <- 5
sd2 <- 1

# Calculate the y values for the second normal distribution using dnorm
y2 <- dnorm(x, mean = mean2, sd = sd2)

# Combine the y values of the two distributions to create a bimodal curve
y <- y1 + y2

# Create a data frame for the x and y values
data <- data.frame(x = x, y = y)

# Create the plot
ggplot(data) +
  geom_line(aes(x = x, y = y), color = "blue", size = 1.5) +
  labs(x = "x", y = "Density") +
  ggtitle("Bimodal Gaussian Curve") +
  theme_minimal()
```

```{r}
library(ggplot2)

# Define the range of x values
x <- seq(0, 1, length.out = 200)

# Define the parameters for the first beta distribution
shape1 <- 8
shape2 <- 15

# Calculate the y values for the first beta distribution using dbeta
y1 <- dbeta(x, shape1, shape2)

# Define the parameters for the second beta distribution
shape3 <- 9
shape4 <- 4

# Calculate the y values for the second beta distribution using dbeta
y2 <- dbeta(x, shape3, shape4)

# Combine the y values of the two distributions to create a bimodal curve
y <- y1 + y2

# Create a data frame for the x and y values
data <- data.frame(x = x, y = y)

# Create the plot
ggplot(data) +
  geom_line(aes(x = x, y = y), color = "blue", size = 1.5) +
  labs(x = "x", y = "Density") +
  geom_function(fun = dnorm, args=list(mean=0.5,sd=.07), lwd=2, color="gray7", alpha=1)+
  #ggtitle("Bimodal Beta Distribution") +
  theme_void()

```
